00011| Welcome to the Next.js documentation!
00012| 
00013| ## What is Next.js?
00014| 
00015| Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.
00016| 
00017| It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.
00018| 
00019| Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.
00020| 
00021| ## How to use the docs
00022| 
00023| The docs are organized into 3 sections:
00024| 
00025| - [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
00026| - [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
00027| - [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.
00028| 
00029| Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.
00030| 
00031| ## App Router and Pages Router
00032| 
00033| Next.js has two different routers:
00034| 
00035| - **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
00036| - **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.
00037| 
00038| At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.
00039| 
00040| ### React version handling
00041| 
00042| The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:
00043| 
00044| - **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.
00045| 
00046| - **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.
00047| 
00048| This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.
00049| 
00050| ## Pre-requisite knowledge
00051| 
00052| Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:
00053| 
00054| - HTML
00055| - CSS
00056| - JavaScript
00057| - React
00058| 
00059| If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.
00060| 
00061| ## Accessibility
00062| 
00063| For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.
00064| 
00065| ## Join our Community
00066| 
00067| If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded.

## Use an AI agent (recommended)

An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded.

Upgrade this app to Next.js 16.

Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:

- **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

[`Headers.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/entries): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object. 00037| - [`Headers.forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/forEach): Executes a provided function once for each key/value pair in this `Headers` object. 00038| - [`Headers.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get): Returns a [`String`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String) sequence of all the values of a header within a `Headers` object with a given name. 00039| - [`Headers.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has): Returns a boolean stating whether a `Headers` object contains a certain header. 00040| - [`Headers.keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/keys): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 00041| - [`Headers.values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/values): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 00042| 00043| ## Good to know 00044| 00045| - `headers` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function. 00046| - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. 00001| ---
00002| title: generateStaticParams
00003| description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
00007| 
00008| `generateStaticParams` can be used with:
00009| 
00010| - [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
00011| - [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
00012| - [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
00013| 
00014| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00015| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00016| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00017|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00018| 
00019|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00020|     slug: post.slug,
00021|   }))
00022| }
00023| 
00024| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00025| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00026| export default async function Page({
00027|   params,
00028| }: {
00029|   params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
00030| }) {
00031|   const { slug } = await params
00032|   // ...
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00037| // Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
00038| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00039|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00040| 
00041|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00042|     slug: post.slug,
00043|   }))
00044| }
00045| 
00046| // Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
00047| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00048| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00049|   const { slug } = await params
00050|   // ...
00051| }
00052| ```
00053| 
00054| > **Good to know**:
00055| >
00056| > - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00057| > - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
00058| > - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
00059| > - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
00060| > - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
00061| > - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
00062| 
00063| ## Parameters
00064| 
00065| `options.params` (optional)
00066| 
00067| If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
00068| 
00069| The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
00070| 
00071| ## Returns
00072| 
00073| `generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
00074| 
00075| - Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
00076| - The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
00077| 
00078| | Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
00079| | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
00080| | `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
00081| | `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
00082| | `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
00083| 
00084| ## Single Dynamic Segment
00085| 
00086| ```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher

00088|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00089| }

00092| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00093| // - /product/1
00094| // - /product/2
00095| // - /product/3
00096| export default async function Page({
00097|   params,
00098| }: {
00099|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
00100| }) {
00101|   const { id } = await params
00102|   // ...
00103| }
00104| ```
00105| 
00106| ```jsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.js" switcher

00113| // - /product/1
00114| // - /product/2
00115| // - /product/3

00117|   const { id } = await params
00118|   // ...
00119| }
00120| ```
00121| 
00122| ## Multiple Dynamic Segments
00123| 
00124| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00125| export function generateStaticParams() {
00126|   return [
00127|     { category: 'a', product: '1' },
00128|     { category: 'b', product: '2' },
00129|     { category: 'c', product: '3' },
00130|   ]
00131| }

00134| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00135| // - /products/a/1
00136| // - /products/b/2
00137| // - /products/c/3

00139|   params,
00140| }: {
00141|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00142| }) {

00144|   // ...
00145| }
00146| ```
00147| 
00148| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher

00151|     { category: 'a', product: '1' },
00152|     { category: 'b', product: '2' },

00168| ## Catch-all Dynamic Segment
00169| 
00170| ```tsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00171| export function generateStaticParams() {
00172|   return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
00173| }
00174| 
00175| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00176| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00177| // - /product/a/1
00178| // - /product/b/2
00179| // - /product/c/3
00180| export default async function Page({
00181|   params,
00182| }: {
00183|   params: Promise<{ slug: string[] }>
00184| }) {

00186|   // ...
00187| }

00189| 
00190| ```jsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.js" switcher

00192|   return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
00193| }
00194|

00196| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00197| // - /product/a/1
00198| // - /product/b/2
00199| // - /product/c/3

00201|   const { slug } = await params
00202|   // ...
00203| }
00204| ```
00205| 
00206| ## Examples
00207| 
00208| ### Prerendering
00209| 
00210| #### All paths at build time
00211| 
00212| To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
00213| 
00214| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00215| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00216|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00217| 
00218|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00219|     slug: post.slug,
00220|   }))
00221| }
00222| ```
00223| 
00224| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00225| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00226|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00227| 
00228|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00229|     slug: post.slug,
00230|   }))
00231| }
00232| ```
00233| 
00234| #### Subset of paths at build time
00235| 
00236| To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
00237| 
00238| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00239| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00240|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00241| 
00242|   // Render the first 10 posts at build time
00243|   return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
00244|     slug: post.slug,
00245|   }))
00246| }
00247| ```
00248| 
00249| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00250| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00251|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00252| 
00253|   // Render the first 10 posts at build time
00254|   return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
00255|     slug: post.slug,
00256|   }))
00257| }
00258| ```
00259| 
00260| Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00261| 
00262| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00263| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00264| export const dynamicParams = false
00265| 
00266| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00267|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00268|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00269| 
00270|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00271|     slug: post.slug,
00272|   }))
00273| }
00274| ```
00275| 
00276| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00277| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00278| export const dynamicParams = false
00279| 
00280| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00281|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00282|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00283| 
00284|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00285|     slug: post.slug,
00286|   }))
00287| }
00288| ```
00289| 
00290| #### All paths at runtime
00291| 
00292| To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
00293| 
00294| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
00295| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00296|   return []
00297| }
00298| ```
00299| 
00300| > **Good to know:**
00301| >
00302| > - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
00303| 
00304| ```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
00305| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00306| ```
00307| 
00308| #### With Cache Components
00309| 
00310| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
00311| 
00312| > **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
00313| 
00314| See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
00315| 
00316| ### With Route Handlers
00317| 
00318| You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
00319| 
00320| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
00321| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00322|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00323| }
00324| 
00325| export async function GET(
00326|   request: Request,
00327|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00328| ) {
00329|   const { id } = await params
00330|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00331|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00332| }
00333| ```
00334| 
00335| ```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
00336| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00337|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00338| }
00339| 
00340| export async function GET(request, { params }) {
00341|   const { id } = await params
00342|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00343|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00344| }
00345| ```
00346| 
00347| ### Route Handlers with Cache Components
00348| 
00349| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
00350| 
00351| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
00352| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00353|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00354| }
00355| 
00356| async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
00357|   'use cache'
00358|   const resolvedId = await id
00359|   const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
00360|   return response.json()
00361| }
00362| 
00363| export async function GET(
00364|   request: Request,
00365|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00366| ) {
00367|   const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
00368|   return Response.json(post)
00369| }
00370| ```
00371| 
00372| See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
00373| 
00374| ### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
00375| 
00376| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
00377| 
00378| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00379| 
00380| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
00381| 
00382| - `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
00383| - `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
00384| 
00385| There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
00386| 
00387| #### Generate params from the bottom up
00388| 
00389| Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
00390| 
00391| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00392| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00393| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00394|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00395| 
00396|   return products.map((product) => ({
00397|     category: product.category.slug,
00398|     product: product.id,
00399|   }))
00400| }
00401| 
00402| export default function Page({
00403|   params,
00404| }: {
00405|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00406| }) {
00407|   // ...
00408| }
00409| ```
00410| 
00411| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00412| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00413| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00414|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00415| 
00416|   return products.map((product) => ({
00417|     category: product.category.slug,
00418|     product: product.id,
00419|   }))
00420| }
00421| 
00422| export default function Page({ params }) {
00423|   // ...
00424| }
00425| ```
00426| 
00427| #### Generate params from the top down
00428| 
00429| Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
00430| 
00431| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
00432| // Generate segments for [category]
00433| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00434|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00435| 
00436|   return products.map((product) => ({
00437|     category: product.category.slug,
00438|   }))
00439| }
00440| 
00441| export default function Layout({
00442|   params,
00443| }: {
00444|   params: Promise<{ category: string }>
00445| }) {
00446|   // ...
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
00451| // Generate segments for [category]
00452| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00453|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00454| 
00455|   return products.map((product) => ({
00456|     category: product.category.slug,
00457|   }))
00458| }
00459| 
00460| export default function Layout({ params }) {
00461|   // ...
00462| }
00463| ```
00464| 
00465| A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
00466| 
00467| The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
00468| 
00469| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00470| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00471| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00472| export async function generateStaticParams({
00473|   params: { category },
00474| }: {
00475|   params: { category: string }
00476| }) {
00477|   const products = await fetch(
00478|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00479|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00480| 
00481|   return products.map((product) => ({
00482|     product: product.id,
00483|   }))
00484| }
00485| 
00486| export default function Page({
00487|   params,
00488| }: {
00489|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00490| }) {
00491|   // ...
00492| }
00493| ```
00494| 
00495| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00496| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00497| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00498| export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
00499|   const products = await fetch(
00500|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00501|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00502| 
00503|   return products.map((product) => ({
00504|     product: product.id,
00505|   }))
00506| }
00507| 
00508| export default function Page({ params }) {
00509|   // ...
00510| }
00511| ```
00512| 
00513| Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
00514| 
00515| > **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
00516| 
00517| For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
00518| 
00519| ```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00520| export async function generateStaticParams({
00521|   params: { category },
00522| }: {
00523|   params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
00524| }) {
00525|   const products = await fetch(
00526|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00527|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00528| 
00529|   return products.map((product) => ({
00530|     product: product.id,
00531|   }))
00532| }
00533| ```
00534| 
00535| > **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00536| 
00537| ## Version History
00538| 
00539| | Version   | Changes                            |
00540| | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
00541| | `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |
00542|

00308| #### With Cache Components
00309| 
00310| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.

00314| See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.

00375| 
00376| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. 00378| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00379| 
00380| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:

00398|     product: product.id,
00399|   }))
00400| }

00403|   params,
00404| }: {
00405|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00406| }) {

00424| }

00428| 
00429| Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
00430| 
00431| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher

00438|   }))
00439| }

00443| }: {

00445| }) {
00446|   // ...
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher

00476| }) {

00479|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00480|

00483|   }))
00484| }

00488| }: {

00129|     { category: 'c', product: '3' },
00130|   ]
00131| }
00132| 
00133| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00134| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00135| // - /products/a/1
00136| // - /products/b/2
00137| // - /products/c/3
00138| export default async function Page({
00139|   params,
00140| }: {
00141|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00142| }) {
00143|   const { category, product } = await params
00144|   // ...
00145| }
00146| ```
00147| 
00148| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00149| export function generateStaticParams() {
00150|   return [
00151|     { category: 'a', product: '1' },
00152|     { category: 'b', product: '2' },
00153|     { category: 'c', product: '3' },
00154|   ]
00155| }
00156| 
00157| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00158| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00159| // - /products/a/1
00160| // - /products/b/2
00161| // - /products/c/3
00162| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00163|   const { category, product } = await params
00164|   // ...
00165| }
00166| ```
00167| 
00168| ## Catch-all Dynamic Segment
00169| 
00170| ```tsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00171| export function generateStaticParams() {
00172|   return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
00173| }
00174| 
00175| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00176| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00177| // - /product/a/1
00178| // - /product/b/2
00179| // - /product/c/3
00180| export default async function Page({
00181|   params,
00182| }: {
00183|   params: Promise<{ slug: string[] }>
00184| }) {
00185|   const { slug } = await params
00186|   // ...
00187| }
00188| ```
00189| 
00190| ```jsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.js" switcher
00191| export function generateStaticParams() {
00192|   return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
00193| }
00194| 
00195| // Three versions of this page will be statically generated
00196| // using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
00197| // - /product/a/1
00198| // - /product/b/2
00199| // - /product/c/3
00200| export default async function Page({ params }) {
00201|   const { slug } = await params
00202|   // ...
00203| }
00204| ```
00205| 
00206| ## Examples
00207| 
00208| ### Prerendering
00209| 
00210| #### All paths at build time
00211| 
00212| To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
00213| 
00214| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00215| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00216|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00217| 
00218|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00219|     slug: post.slug,
00220|   }))
00221| }
00222| ```
00223| 
00224| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00225| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00226|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00227| 
00228|   return posts.map((post) => ({
00229|     slug: post.slug,
00230|   }))
00231| }
00232| ```
00233| 
00234| #### Subset of paths at build time
00235| 
00236| To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
00237| 
00238| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00239| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00240|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00241| 
00242|   // Render the first 10 posts at build time
00243|   return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
00244|     slug: post.slug,
00245|   }))
00246| }
00247| ```
00248| 
00249| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00250| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00251|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00252| 
00253|   // Render the first 10 posts at build time
00254|   return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
00255|     slug: post.slug,
00256|   }))
00257| }
00258| ```
00259| 
00260| Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
00261| 
00262| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
00263| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00264| export const dynamicParams = false
00265| 
00266| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00267|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00268|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00269| 
00270|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00271|     slug: post.slug,
00272|   }))
00273| }
00274| ```
00275| 
00276| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
00277| // All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
00278| export const dynamicParams = false
00279| 
00280| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00281|   const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
00282|   const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
00283| 
00284|   return topPosts.map((post) => ({
00285|     slug: post.slug,
00286|   }))
00287| }
00288| ```
00289| 
00290| #### All paths at runtime
00291| 
00292| To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
00293| 
00294| ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
00295| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00296|   return []
00297| }
00298| ```
00299| 
00300| > **Good to know:**
00301| >
00302| > - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
00303| 
00304| ```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
00305| export const dynamic = 'force-static'
00306| ```
00307| 
00308| #### With Cache Components
00309| 
00310| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
00311| 
00312| > **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
00313| 
00314| See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
00315| 
00316| ### With Route Handlers
00317| 
00318| You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
00319| 
00320| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
00321| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00322|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00323| }
00324| 
00325| export async function GET(
00326|   request: Request,
00327|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00328| ) {
00329|   const { id } = await params
00330|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00331|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00332| }
00333| ```
00334| 
00335| ```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
00336| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00337|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00338| }
00339| 
00340| export async function GET(request, { params }) {
00341|   const { id } = await params
00342|   // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
00343|   return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
00344| }
00345| ```
00346| 
00347| ### Route Handlers with Cache Components
00348| 
00349| When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
00350| 
00351| ```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
00352| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00353|   return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
00354| }
00355| 
00356| async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
00357|   'use cache'
00358|   const resolvedId = await id
00359|   const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
00360|   return response.json()
00361| }
00362| 
00363| export async function GET(
00364|   request: Request,
00365|   { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
00366| ) {
00367|   const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
00368|   return Response.json(post)
00369| }
00370| ```
00371| 
00372| See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
00373| 
00374| ### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
00375| 
00376| To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
00377| 
00378| ### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
00379| 
00380| You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
00381| 
00382| - `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
00383| - `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
00384| 
00385| There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
00386| 
00387| #### Generate params from the bottom up
00388| 
00389| Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
00390| 
00391| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00392| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00393| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00394|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00395| 
00396|   return products.map((product) => ({
00397|     category: product.category.slug,
00398|     product: product.id,
00399|   }))
00400| }
00401| 
00402| export default function Page({
00403|   params,
00404| }: {
00405|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00406| }) {
00407|   // ...
00408| }
00409| ```
00410| 
00411| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00412| // Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
00413| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00414|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00415| 
00416|   return products.map((product) => ({
00417|     category: product.category.slug,
00418|     product: product.id,
00419|   }))
00420| }
00421| 
00422| export default function Page({ params }) {
00423|   // ...
00424| }
00425| ```
00426| 
00427| #### Generate params from the top down
00428| 
00429| Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
00430| 
00431| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
00432| // Generate segments for [category]
00433| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00434|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00435| 
00436|   return products.map((product) => ({
00437|     category: product.category.slug,
00438|   }))
00439| }
00440| 
00441| export default function Layout({
00442|   params,
00443| }: {
00444|   params: Promise<{ category: string }>
00445| }) {
00446|   // ...
00447| }
00448| ```
00449| 
00450| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
00451| // Generate segments for [category]
00452| export async function generateStaticParams() {
00453|   const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
00454| 
00455|   return products.map((product) => ({
00456|     category: product.category.slug,
00457|   }))
00458| }
00459| 
00460| export default function Layout({ params }) {
00461|   // ...
00462| }
00463| ```
00464| 
00465| A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
00466| 
00467| The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
00468| 
00469| ```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00470| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00471| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00472| export async function generateStaticParams({
00473|   params: { category },
00474| }: {
00475|   params: { category: string }
00476| }) {
00477|   const products = await fetch(
00478|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00479|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00480| 
00481|   return products.map((product) => ({
00482|     product: product.id,
00483|   }))
00484| }
00485| 
00486| export default function Page({
00487|   params,
00488| }: {
00489|   params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
00490| }) {
00491|   // ...
00492| }
00493| ```
00494| 
00495| ```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
00496| // Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
00497| // the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
00498| export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
00499|   const products = await fetch(
00500|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00501|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00502| 
00503|   return products.map((product) => ({
00504|     product: product.id,
00505|   }))
00506| }
00507| 
00508| export default function Page({ params }) {
00509|   // ...
00510| }
00511| ```
00512| 
00513| Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
00514| 
00515| > **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
00516| 
00517| For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
00518| 
00519| ```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
00520| export async function generateStaticParams({
00521|   params: { category },
00522| }: {
00523|   params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
00524| }) {
00525|   const products = await fetch(
00526|     `https://.../products?category=${category}`
00527|   ).then((res) => res.json())
00528| 
00529|   return products.map((product) => ({
00530|     product: product.id,
00531|   }))
00532| }
00533| ```
00534| 
00535| > **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00536| 
00537| ## Version History
00538| 
00539| | Version   | Changes                            |
00540| | --------- | ---------------------------------- |
00541| | `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |
00542|

00005| 
00006| The `useRouter` hook allows you to programmatically change routes inside [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).
00007| 
00008| > **Recommendation:** Use the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) for navigation unless you have a specific requirement for using `useRouter`.

00014|

00017|

00020|       Dashboard

00027| 'use client'
00028|

00042| ## `useRouter()`
00043| 
00044| - `router.push(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route. Adds a new entry into the [browser's history stack](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/History_API). The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
00045| - `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
00046| - `router.refresh()`: Refresh the current route. Making a new request to the server, re-fetching data requests, and re-rendering Server Components. The client will merge the updated React Server Component payload without losing unaffected client-side React (e.g. `useState`) or browser state (e.g. scroll position). This clears the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) for the current route, but does **not** invalidate the server-side cache. Use [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to invalidate server-side cached data.
00047| - `router.prefetch(href: string, options?: { onInvalidate?: () => void })`: [Prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) the provided route for faster client-side transitions. The optional `onInvalidate` callback is called when the [prefetched data becomes stale](/docs/app/guides/prefetching#extending-or-ejecting-link).
00048| - `router.back()`: Navigate back to the previous route in the browser’s history stack.
00049| - `router.forward()`: Navigate forwards to the next page in the browser’s history stack.
00050| - `router.bfcacheId`: An opaque string identifier scoped to the current route segment. It changes when the surrounding segment is freshly created by a push or replace navigation, and stays the same for back/forward navigations, `router.refresh()`, and search-param- or hash-only navigations. See [`bfcacheId`](#bfcacheid) below for details.
00051| 
00052| > **Good to know**:
00053| >
00054| > - You must not send untrusted or unsanitized URLs to `router.push` or `router.replace`, as this can open your site to cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. For example, `javascript:` URLs sent to `router.push` or `router.replace` will be executed in the context of your page.
00055| > - The `<Link>` component automatically prefetch routes as they become visible in the viewport.
00056| > - `refresh()` could re-produce the same result if fetch requests are cached. Other Request-time APIs like `cookies` and `headers` could also change the response.

 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally

 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be

The `notFound` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 404 page. It's useful for handling missing resources in your application. You can customize the UI using the [`not-found.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found).

Invoking `notFound()` throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` error and terminates rendering of the route segment where it was thrown. Next.js also injects a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` tag so the page is not indexed. Because it works by throwing, call it in the render path: a component, or a function a component `await`s. A call left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, and no not-found UI renders (in development the server logs `⨯ unhandledRejection: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404`).

`notFound()` can be invoked in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), and [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

description: API Reference for the notFound function.
related:

    - app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized

The `notFound` function throws an error that renders a Next.js 404 page. It's useful for handling missing resources in your application. You can customize the UI using the [`not-found.js` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found).

Invoking `notFound()` throws a `NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404` error and terminates rendering of the route segment where it was thrown. Next.js also injects a `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` tag so the page is not indexed. Because it works by throwing, call it in the render path: a component, or a function a component `await`s. A call left in an un-awaited promise throws where nothing catches it, and no not-found UI renders (in development the server logs `⨯ unhandledRejection: NEXT_HTTP_ERROR_FALLBACK;404`).

`notFound()` can be invoked in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), and [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

events.content:
Migration complete. `pages/` is removed and replaced by an App Router tree:

- `app/layout.tsx` — root layout (replaces `_app.js` + `_document.js`); global `<head>` migrated to `metadata` export and `next/font/google` for Inter
- `app/page.tsx` — `getServerSideProps` → async Server Component using `headers()` from `next/headers`
- `app/blog/page.tsx` — `getStaticProps` + `revalidate: 60` → `fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: 60 } })`
- `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` — `getStaticPaths` → `generateStaticParams`; `notFound: true` → `notFound()` from `next/navigation`; `next/head` → `generateMetadata`
- `app/api/posts/route.ts` + `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` — Pages API → Route Handlers with named HTTP method exports (`GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE`), Web `Request`/`NextResponse`
- `app/not-found.tsx` — replaces `pages/404.js`
- `app/error.tsx` — replaces `pages/_error.js` (Client Component, uses `error`/`retry` props)
- `components/AppProvider.tsx` — converted to a `'use client'` component with typed context
- Button-driven `router.push` / `router.back` calls extracted into small `'use client'` files (`view-all-posts-button.tsx`, `blog/read-more-button.tsx`, `blog/[id]/back-button.tsx`, `go-home-button.tsx`) using `useRouter` from `next/navigation`

`tsc --noEmit` and `next build` both pass; the build report shows the expected route types (ISR `1m` on `/blog`, SSG with 5-min revalidate on first 10 `/blog/[id]`, dynamic on `/` due to `headers()`).
